title: Square Flower (a loop inside a loop)
body:
Goal: draw 8 squares, each turned a little, in 8 different colors. Together they make a flower.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. It draws ONE square.
  2. Put the square loop inside a new loop: 
    for color in PALETTE:
    t.color(color)
    (the square loop goes here, pushed in 4 MORE spaces)
    t.left(45)
  3. Press Run (F5). Tip: t.speed(0) makes the turtle draw super fast.

Why 45? There are 8 colors in the palette, and 8 x 45 = 360: one full turn.

Done looks like: 8 squares in 8 colors, spinning round the middle.

Extra: try t.left(30) with for i in range(12): instead. Or make the squares into triangles!

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the # TODO comment at the bottom of starter.py. It shows a new loop that goes around the square loop. The square loop you already have stays, but it moves inside.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Write a for loop that goes through every color in PALETTE. The first line inside it sets the color. Then the square loop goes inside, pushed in by 4 more spaces. Last, turn a little before the next square starts.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Start with for color in ____: and put t.color(____) right under it. The old for side in range(4): loop comes next, pushed in 4 spaces, with its own lines pushed in 4 more. Finish with t.left(____), lined up with t.color.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Square Flower - a loop inside a loop

import turtle

# The color-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette: 8 colors everyone can tell apart
PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442",
           "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"]

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.shape("turtle")
t.pensize(3)
t.speed(0)

t.color(PALETTE[4])

# This loop draws ONE square.
for side in range(4):
    t.forward(100)
    t.left(90)

# TODO: put the square loop INSIDE a new loop, like this:
#   for color in PALETTE:
#       t.color(color)
#       ...the square loop, pushed in 4 more spaces...
#       t.left(45)

turtle.done()
